title: 2D and 3D physics
summary: Connect entities to 2D or 3D bodies and keep simulation stepping, interaction and cleanup consistent.

blocks.text: Construct the world with a scene

Physics2D and Physics3D are scene-aware controllers, not IPlugin objects. Construct them with a Scene and an options object; register entities with add/addMany. Use `motion: "static" | "dynamic" | "kinematic"`. The term fixed appears in some external physics APIs, but the Retiam options use static.

blocks.text: Physics3D.ready waits for backend initialization when supported. The 2D wrapper has no corresponding ready method; Rapier initialization lives in its backend. Do not call methods on a WASM world before the specific backend has completed readiness.

The current Box3D backend explicitly uses box3d-wasm/standard: a single-threaded WebAssembly build with SIMD. It does not create worker threads or require cross-origin isolation, so it is suitable for static hosts such as GitHub Pages.

blocks.content: Physics3D.addSoftBody throws when the selected backend has no soft-body method. Its error suggests Jolt, but the current controller does not select Jolt. Treat 3D soft bodies through that controller as unavailable until backend routing and exports are implemented.

blocks.text: Physics step parameters are seconds. Physics2D auto-step calls a fixed timeStep times scene.timeScale on each update; it is not a wall-clock accumulator in the wrapper. Physics3D auto-step currently multiplies the already scene-scaled dt by scene.timeScale again. These details matter when changing frame rate or timeScale.

For a controlled simulation, set autoStep false and implement a fixed-step accumulator using dt/1000 with one intentional timeScale policy. Bound the number of catch-up steps. Keep the composer updating and use the same fixed step for preview and offline output when comparing trajectories.

The backends infer common colliders from primitives and expose additional mesh/convex choices through options. RigidBody components synchronize physical transforms to the scene graph. Move a kinematic body through the supported component/backend API instead of fighting a dynamic body’s per-frame position sync.

CollisionStart/End listeners receive entities and body components. Sensors/triggers detect overlap without normal collision response. Friction, restitution, damping, CCD, mass and density affect different parts of the solver. Collider decomposition and triangle meshes are backend-sensitive; inspect the relevant adapter for supported dynamic shapes.

2D joints include revolute, distance/spring, fixed, prismatic and rope. Add physical bodies before connecting a joint. FrequencyHz and dampingRatio are converted to backend-specific spring coefficients; addSpring returns both the joint and a visual Spring that follows the bodies. Mouse dragging uses backend point lookup and a spring-like mouse constraint.

SoftBody2DComponent constructs radial or grid particle/spring lattices and updates vector geometry from their positions. Lattice resolution, particle mass and spring parameters change both visual deformation and solver cost.
